A figured-bass framework gives the left hand a bass line with chord figures to realize, so the player builds full chords above a singing bass. The form runs Statement, Realization, Variation, Closing across 32 bars, with 320 notes for both hands and a total playing time of 83.5 seconds. To play it, realize each chord fully above the bass, keep the bass line singing, and voice the top note of each chord. The framework itself belongs to the public musical language, while this melodic realization is original and is not attributed to any composer.

A gigue framework is a lively closing dance with a driving, bouncing rhythm, the hands trading quick figures over a firm bass. The form runs First Strain, Second Strain, Return, Closing across 32 bars, with 320 notes for both hands and a total playing time of 66.2 seconds. To play it, keep the bounce light, articulate the quick figures evenly, and drive toward each phrase ending. The framework itself belongs to the public musical language, while this melodic realization is original and is not attributed to any composer.
